title: Homelessness funding deferred; affordable housing on regional land approved
subtitle: Also: 36 hybrid buses, student transit passes, Conestoga College transit hub, Mobility Plus targets and respiratory season update.
overview: Regional Council deferred a decision on how to spend the new $10.2 million for the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. A motion to spread the money proportionally across all items was moved, but Council instead voted to bring it back to a special meeting on February 6 {{vote:m10}}. Concerns centred on unclear direction from the budget debate and on a lack of consultation with area municipalities.

Council unanimously asked staff to study affordable housing on regionally owned land, including parking lots, vacant properties and buildings that could be repurposed {{vote:m13}}. Several delegates spoke in support. Council also approved the pre-budget purchase of 36 hybrid transit buses {{vote:m5}} and a package of transit items: a Conestoga College hub design, new U-Pass agreements through August 2027, and Mobility Plus targets {{vote:m7}}.

Council also approved a 90 per cent refinancing limit for regional affordable housing projects and an addendum to the Multi-Year Accessibility Plan {{vote:m8}}. The Chair noted upcoming remembrance dates and offered condolences for former Regional Councillor Jim Wideman.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the allocation of the new $10.2 million for the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness to a Special Council meeting on February 6, 2024 {{vote:m10}}.

Council asked staff to include regionally owned parking lots, vacant properties and re-purposable buildings in affordable housing plans and to report on locations, ownership options, concepts and partners.
Council approved the pre-budget procurement of 36 hybrid transit buses from Nova Bus Inc. at an estimated $43,181,964 plus taxes.

decisions.item: Transit hub, U-Pass and Mobility Plus
decisions.detail: Council approved the Conestoga College transit hub design, a consulting increase of $357,000, U-Pass agreements to August 2027, a 2.5% undelivered-trip target for Mobility Plus in 2024, and an in-year report on scheduling software.
Council set total encumbrances at 90 per cent for Regionally funded affordable housing projects that permit secondary financing, and authorized staff to execute refinancing agreements.
Council approved an addendum to the 2023-2027 Multi-Year Accessibility Plan and wrote off $31,181.52 in accounts receivable for 2023.

debate: On the homelessness budget, staff said both options were needed and advised against choosing between line items, since all items were required in 2024. Staff also said area municipalities were not consulted after the budget decision.

Some councillors said both options were difficult. They noted the $10.2 million is new money, and that the fee-for-service funding was for new programs that did not exist in 2023. One councillor noted that only a project that did not meet the original criteria would receive its full request.

Those favouring deferral said the budget-day motions were unclear and they had unanswered questions. Others said delay was unfair to organizations waiting for funding. An amendment to protect fee-for-service funding was withdrawn after staff said the reserve it relied on was almost fully committed.

Delegates on housing over parking argued that public land lets governments control affordability and that finding sites is the main barrier. One suggested a quick pilot project alongside a larger strategy. Councillors noted the Region already has surplus-land housing projects.
Two delegates criticized the reduced homelessness funding, citing food bank and waitlist data and comparing it with the police budget increase.
